Algorithm — A finite, unambiguous procedure for solving a problem.
Anaesthesia — Controlled loss of sensation, with or without unconsciousness, for medical procedures.
Antibiotic — Drug that kills bacteria or inhibits their growth.
Antisepsis — Use of chemicals on living tissue to reduce microorganisms.
Asepsis — Practices that prevent contamination by microorganisms.
Bayes’ theorem — Rule for updating probability using new evidence.
Calculus — Mathematics of change and accumulation.
Capacity factor — Actual energy output divided by maximum possible output over a period.
Cell theory — Principle that organisms consist of cells and cells arise from pre-existing cells.
Clinical trial — Controlled study of a medical intervention in people.
Cold chain — Temperature-controlled supply system for sensitive products.
CRISPR — Gene-editing technology derived from microbial immune systems.
CT — Computed tomography using X-rays to reconstruct cross-sectional images.
Digital signature — Cryptographic method supporting authenticity and integrity.
DNA — Molecule carrying hereditary information in most organisms.
Dual-use — Technology capable of beneficial and harmful applications.
Electromagnetic induction — Generation of voltage by changing magnetic flux.
Entropy — Measure associated with energy dispersal and the direction of processes; also used analogously in information theory.
Epidemiology — Study of disease patterns and causes in populations.
Fission — Splitting of a heavy atomic nucleus.
Gene therapy — Treatment that changes genetic material or its expression.
Geostationary orbit — Circular equatorial orbit in which a satellite appears fixed over Earth.
Germ theory — Theory that microorganisms cause many diseases.
Graph theory — Mathematics of nodes and links.
Green hydrogen — Hydrogen produced by renewable-powered electrolysis.
Herd immunity — Indirect protection when enough people are immune to reduce transmission.
Innovation — Successful application of a new or improved idea.
Insulin — Hormone regulating blood glucose; used to treat diabetes.
Ionizing radiation — Radiation energetic enough to remove electrons from atoms.
Laser — Device producing coherent amplified light.
Linear programming — Optimization of a linear objective under linear constraints.
MRI — Magnetic resonance imaging using magnetic fields and radiofrequency signals.
Nanotechnology — Engineering at roughly the 1–100 nanometre scale.
Natural selection — Differential survival and reproduction of heritable variations.
Nuclear medicine — Use of radioactive tracers or materials in diagnosis and treatment.
Optimization — Selection of the best feasible solution.
Patent — Time-limited legal right over a qualifying invention in exchange for disclosure.
PCR — Method for rapidly amplifying selected DNA.
Peer review — Expert evaluation of scholarly work before publication.
Penicillin — First widely used major antibiotic class, originating from Penicillium mould.
Photovoltaic effect — Conversion of light into electrical energy in a material.
Place value — Numeral system in which position determines value.
Public health — Protection and improvement of health at population level.
Quantum bit — Basic unit of quantum information.
Radioactivity — Spontaneous emission from unstable atomic nuclei.
Raman effect — Inelastic scattering of light that reveals molecular information.
Randomization — Assignment by chance to reduce bias in experiments.
Relativity — Einstein’s theories linking space, time, motion and gravity.
Replication — Independent repetition of a study or result.
Satellite — Object placed in orbit around a celestial body.
Scientific law — Concise description of a regular natural pattern.
Semiconductor — Material whose electrical conductivity can be controlled.
Standard deviation — Measure of spread around a mean.
Statistics — Science of learning from data.
Stem cell — Cell capable of self-renewal and differentiation.
Technology transfer — Movement of knowledge from research into practical use.
Transistor — Semiconductor device used to switch or amplify signals.
Ultrasound — Imaging or measurement using high-frequency sound waves.
Vaccination — Administration of a vaccine to induce immune protection.
Valley of death — Gap between promising research and scalable adoption.
X-ray — Ionizing electromagnetic radiation used in imaging and analysis.
Zero — Number representing no quantity and a placeholder in positional notation.
